missionPremise: Gap ledger section 11: wells (tx_rrc_well, 1,396,049 rows statewide) and special districts including MUD (tx_special_district, 2,775 rows, 1,888 MUD) were unaccounted on every parcel_record row. Ingest both as companion rails, zone-major spatial, with swept-no-hit parcels earning absent-verified (the sweep is the look) and unswept parcels staying unaccounted.
completionPredicate: Met, with the implementation, testing, and full production execution already performed by a parallel property-seat session before this seat claimed the card (this close formalizes and independently verifies that work rather than repeating it). Both wells and specialDistricts ingested for all six program counties; Caldwell correctly shows a total noGeom sweep miss (the same pre-existing txgio geometry gap PARCEL-R3-FLOOD already found); a genuine correctness defect (single-fragment parcels undercounting multi-tile parcels by ~1%) was found and fixed before the production run, not after; an initial per-row write pattern that could not complete in reasonable time was found and fixed (batched) before the production run completed. This seat re-ran the full test suite fresh (548/550 pass), ran an independent sample-based cross-check against live data (2.80% vs the job's 2.08%, consistent given non-random sampling), and directly spot-checked the gold parcel's cell and companion-row state in the Factory store.

whatContradictedTheCard: The dispatch's own premise ('point-major LATERAL is ~218x slower... a named dead-end') does not correspond to any figure actually in this repo -- the implementing session checked and found only this seat's own 27.6x flood-ingest figure, which favors the OPPOSITE approach (direct join, not materialization) for a structurally different source (a native-geometry, GiST-indexed table vs jsonb-encoded polygons with no index). The zone-major materialized pattern used here is justified on its own grounds (p2-juris's prior, separately-proven need to decode complex jsonb polygons once rather than per row) rather than by trusting the cited figure -- exactly the 'EXPLAIN ANALYZE both plans before committing' discipline a planner addendum on this card asked for, already satisfied before this seat ever saw the addendum.

A parcel spanning multiple txgio_parcel tile fragments (15% of Bastrop) was undercounted by the single-fragment-pick pattern this seat's own flood-ingest.mjs and the pre-existing p2-juris-store.mjs both use -- live-measured at ~1% of matched wells missed. Fixed here by unioning all fragments per prop_id; flood-ingest.mjs was left untouched (out of this card's scope) and is flagged as sharing this exposure.

The first live --apply attempt (per-row writes) was cancelled after 9+ minutes on the smallest county with no end in sight -- a real, measured scaling failure, not a hypothetical, found and fixed (batched writes) before the successful production run.
constraintsHonored: zone-major spatial pattern used, with its own justification stated rather than assumed from the card's premise
MUD not treated as a separate rail (district_type is a payload field, not a rail key)
swept-no-hit correctly emits absent-verified with the sweep as basis; the gold parcel spot-check confirms this live
Cloud Run only for every write
Caldwell excluded/naturally handled as noGeom rather than forced or faked

LESSON: When claiming a card whose worktree already shows merged work on main, read the actual code and PR history before assuming the card needs to be built from scratch -- this card's real remaining work was independent verification and closing the loop, not implementation.

A correctness finding from one card (multi-fragment parcel undercounting) can retroactively apply to an EARLIER, already-closed card's own code (this seat's own flood-ingest.mjs) -- worth checking newer siblings' designs against older closed work even after the fact, not just newer work against older lessons.
